$comment: Contract for workspace/reports/callgraph_dag.json, written by scripts/build_callgraph_dag.py from the Phase 0 model (plan steps I5a/I5b, I7, I8; remediation R4). Strict on what consumers read (scripts/module_map.py, pipeline_make.py, harness_reach.py, ledger.py, wp_scheduler.py): the module, sub-module and function maps, their membership lists, run flags and fallback markers. Other fields stay open: the producer adds facts over time. `schema_version` is stamped by block_fallback_units (DAG_SCHEMA_VERSION): a link-unit DAG without it predates the GCC-fallback blocking (defect 6), which validate_artifacts.py run-dir reports.

module.$comment: A DAG module: a link unit (module_kind link_unit) or a path module. `functions` are DAG keys.

unit_visibility.$comment: External visibility class of a non-test link unit carried from phase0_model.json

callgraph_fallback.$comment: Frama-C's first error for a unit on the GCC fallback

linked_modules.$comment: project DAG module names this link unit transitively links

ldflags.$comment: link options for the libraries the unit links from outside the project (build_callgraph_dag.unit_link_options)

threat_model_entries.$comment: FRAMAC_HARNESS_SCOPE_V2: unit functions explicitly listed in THREAT_MODEL.md input_sources

deferred_non_attacker_entries.$comment: FRAMAC_HARNESS_SCOPE_V2: exported/vtable entries excluded from fuzzing by THREAT_MODEL.md trusted_callers or non-attacker role (kept in DAG/ledger for WP)

harness_scope_note.$comment: FRAMAC_HARNESS_SCOPE_V2: why a unit has no direct harness entry points (e.g. internal_convenience_covered_by_consumers)

cross_cluster_unclustered.$comment: unit-reachable functions dropped into unclustered because producer and consumer clusters could not merge within limits

over_limit.$comment: the sub-modules over the split's thresholds (`over_limit` on each)

fuzz_engine_reason.$comment: why the DAG chose `fuzz_engine`: the GCC fallback, or setjmp/longjmp (route_nonlocal_jumps)

submodule.$comment: A cluster of a split link unit (scripts/unit_split.py).

reach.$comment: how its functions were reached from its anchors: address_flow (the model's schema 6 facts) or call_graph (every edge)

over_limit.$comment: why it exceeds the split's thresholds: a single entry point reaching more than one Eva run can take

globals.$comment: address_flow: the global variables its code and their initializers name

build_sources.$comment: address_flow: the .c files its builds compile (its functions' and its globals' files)

link_stubs.$comment: address_flow: unit symbols those files name and do not define, none reachable from its harness; functions are linked as aborting stubs, globals defined zero-initialized

function.$comment: A function, keyed by plain name, or `file#name` when the name collides.

compiled_in.$comment: the .c translation unit(s) compiling a non-.c (.inc/.h) definition (build_capture.json)

indirect_callees.$comment: Dump schema 6: callees reached only through an indirect site's type match

address_refs.$comment: Dump schema 6: project functions whose address this function body takes

global_refs.$comment: Dump schema 6: project global_variables ids this function body names

callgraph_fallback.$comment: Frama-C's first error for a unit compiling it

eva_wp_blocked.$comment: why Eva and WP cannot run on it (its home unit is on the GCC fallback)

model_only.$comment: why the real build does not define it although Frama-C's parse does (build_callgraph_dag.model_only_functions): kept out of harness sources and reach-gate entry points

build_only_functions.$comment: per source file, the functions the build's objects define that Frama-C's parse lacks (build_callgraph_dag.build_only_functions); the link repair places their symbols

model_only_functions.$comment: per file, the DAG keys of the functions Frama-C's parse has and the real build does not define (`model_only` on each function)

global_variables.$comment: the model's global variables with what their initializers name (dump schema 6), function ids as DAG keys; the unit split's address-flow reach reads them
